web.title: Set a custom domain | GitBook Documentation
web.description:
This page is also available as [Markdown](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain.md).

This page shows how to configure a custom domain and subdomain.

You can customize this by setting a custom domain, meaning your audience can access your documentation on a chosen domain.
web.markdown:
[New: The GitBook MCP server is here.\\
\\
Connect your AI agent](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/gitbook-mcp)

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://gitbook.com/docs/llms.txt). This page is also available as [Markdown](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain.md).

This page shows how to configure a custom domain and subdomain. If you would like to configure a custom subdirectory (such as `example.com/docs`), see the [Setting a custom subdirectory](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain/setting-a-custom-subdirectory) page.

GitBook Assistant

By default, your sites are accessible on a `[subdomain].gitbook.io` domain.

GitBook Assistant

You can customize this by setting a custom domain, meaning your audience can access your documentation on a chosen domain.

GitBook Assistant

1

#### Choose a subdomain[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain\#choose-a-subdomain)

When choosing a subdomain, you can either use `www` or a custom one. Some commonly used subdomains are:

GitBook Assistant

- `docs.example.com`



GitBook Assistant

- `help.example.com`



GitBook Assistant

- `developers.example.com`



GitBook Assistant


2

#### Initiate the custom domain setup[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain\#initiate-the-custom-domain-setup)

Navigate to the site for which you want to set the custom domain. Click **Settings,** then choose **Set up a custom domain.**

GitBook Assistant

From here, you'll see a window where you can enter the custom domain you chose in the first step. Type it out and click **Next.**

GitBook Assistant

3

#### Configure the DNS[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain\#configure-the-dns)

At this stage, you'll see a window with three fields: **Type, Name, Target.**

GitBook Assistant

Those are the details you'll use to set your custom domain in your DNS provider. This is done _outside_ GitBook, in the provider you are using for your domain.

GitBook Assistant

Copy the contents of the **Name** and **Target** fields to use in your DNS provider. Each provider is different, so when in doubt, check directly with them how to add this record. You should be able to pick the **Type** of record from a list in your provider.

GitBook Assistant

After adding the record, it might take some time for the changes to propagate. We recommend **waiting at least 1 hour** before moving to the next step. Click **Next** when you are ready.

GitBook Assistant

4

#### Finalize your setup[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain\#finalize-your-setup)

After adding the record and it being propagated, it's time to go live! GitBook will verify the domain, the record you added and will automatically configure the SSL certificate for your domain.

GitBook Assistant

Once done, you'll receive a notification and can click **Finish**. You can also close the window if you need, and we'll send you a notification once the process is done on our side.

GitBook Assistant

### Change or update your custom domain[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain\#change-or-update-your-custom-domain)

To change the custom domain for a site, open the site's **Settings**, under **General** in the site sidebar, and click **Domain and URL**. You can remove the current domain and add a new one, or edit the existing configuration.

GitBook Assistant

Remember to update the DNS settings with your domain provider to point to the new GitBook configuration — the process is the same as the initial setup, with a CNAME record pointing to the value GitBook provides.

GitBook Assistant

### Troubleshooting[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain\#troubleshooting)

Setting up a custom domain can occasionally run into obstacles. Below, we outline frequent problems encountered during this process and provide detailed solutions to each of them.

GitBook Assistant

My custom subdomain isn't working. [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain#my-custom-subdomain-isnt-working)

Custom domain issues are usually DNS-related. Check your DNS configuration:

GitBook Assistant

1. Verify you created a **CNAME record** (not an A record) pointing to the value GitBook provided.



GitBook Assistant

2. Ensure you're using the subdomain format (`docs.yoursite.com` or `www.yoursite.com`).



GitBook Assistant

3. If you use Cloudflare, disable the proxy (orange cloud) — the record must be set to "DNS only".



GitBook Assistant


Common DNS issues:

GitBook Assistant

- **Conflicting records** — remove any existing A, AAAA, or other records for the same subdomain.



GitBook Assistant

- **TTL delays** — DNS changes can take up to 48 hours to propagate globally.



GitBook Assistant

- **CAA records** — if you have CAA records, add `0 issue "pki.goog"` to allow GitBook's SSL certificates.



GitBook Assistant


To test your setup, use a DNS lookup tool like [WhatsMyDNS](https://www.whatsmydns.net/#CNAME) to verify your CNAME record points to the correct GitBook address. If issues persist after 48 hours, contact support with your domain name and the CNAME value GitBook provided.

GitBook Assistant

SSL error: an error occurred when provisioning your SSL certificate. [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain#ssl-error-an-error-occurred-when-provisioning-your-ssl-certificate)

When a custom domain is set for your organization, group, or section, we set up an SSL certificate on our end so that your documentation will load securely, over HTTPS.

This happens automatically when you set your custom domain — you do not need to purchase or configure an SSL certificate.

GitBook Assistant

Occasionally errors occur at this stage, usually when the CNAME record for the custom domain hasn't propagated.

GitBook Assistant

In these cases, we can recommend the following:

GitBook Assistant

1. Check that your CNAME record is set up correctly.
Please review our page about configuring DNS to help you with this.
If the CNAME record is incorrect, we won't be able to configure the SSL certificate and complete the custom domain set-up.



GitBook Assistant

2. Allow _**at least one hour**_ between configuring the CNAME record and finalizing the custom domain setup.



GitBook Assistant

3. Verify if the CNAME has propagated. You can try using a third-party DNS lookup tool, such as [WhatsMyDNS](https://www.whatsmydns.net/), to find out what the servers believe to be correct for your correct CNAME record.



GitBook Assistant

4. If you are using Cloudflare, please confirm that you don’t have the record proxied [as explained here](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/setup/manage-domains/pause-cloudflare/#disable-proxy-on-dns-records).



GitBook Assistant


Domain already connected error: your subdomain is already configured for different content. [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/custom-domain#domain-already-connected-error-your-subdomain-is-already-configured-for-different-content)

A custom domain assigned to a site must be unique. Attempting to use the same custom domain in more than one location will result in an error.

GitBook Assistant

If this happens, you can click the link within the error message to look at the content the custom domain is already connected to. This may help you to decide what to do next.

GitBook Assistant

It’s also possible that you might not have access to the content — if that’s the case, contact the support team and they can help you with your next steps.

GitBook Assistant

The solution to this error will always be one of two things, however:

GitBook Assistant

1. Choose a different custom domain; or



GitBook Assistant

2. Disconnect the custom domain from the content it is already connected to, then reconnect it to the new content.



GitBook Assistant


Last updated 22 days ago

Was this helpful?

web.description:
### Configure the site with gitbook-docs.yaml[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration#configure-the-site-with-gitbook-docs.yaml)
It lives in the Git Sync Project directory.
web.markdown:
[New: The GitBook MCP server is here.\\
\\
Connect your AI agent](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/gitbook-mcp)

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://gitbook.com/docs/llms.txt). This page is also available as [Markdown](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration.md).

Git Sync uses three files. Choose the file that controls the part of Git Sync you need:

GitBook Assistant

- `gitbook-docs.yaml` configures the site and maps spaces to repository directories.



GitBook Assistant

- `.gitbook.yaml` configures how GitBook reads one space’s content.



GitBook Assistant

- `SUMMARY.md` defines a space’s navigation.



GitBook Assistant


### Configure the site with gitbook-docs.yaml[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration\#configure-the-site-with-gitbook-docs.yaml)

`gitbook-docs.yaml` configures the entire site. It lives in the Git Sync Project directory. GitBook uses the repository root when you don't set a **Project directory**.

GitBook Assistant

Use `gitbook-docs.yaml` to define your site structure and map each space to a directory. Each item in `site.structure` has a stable `key`. A space’s `content.directory` sets its repository directory. If a space in a site does not sync to the site’s repository, its `content.directory` is `null`.

GitBook Assistant

#### Keys identify your spaces[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration\#keys-identify-your-spaces)

Git Sync recognizes each space and section by its `key`, not by its title, path, or directory. The key is how GitBook matches an entry in `gitbook-docs.yaml` to existing content from one sync to the next.

GitBook Assistant

**Changing a space’s**`key` **replaces that space.** GitBook treats the old key as removed and the new key as a new space. It creates a new space, imports your content into it from the mapped directory, and leaves the original space in your organization, detached from the site.

GitBook Assistant

Your pages come back, but in a new space with a new space ID. Links, cards, and API calls that reference the old ID stop resolving, and anything that exists only in GitBook rather than in your repository stays with the original space.

GitBook Assistant

Restoring the original key doesn’t undo this. It creates another new space and imports into that one.

GitBook Assistant

Keys are safe to choose freely when you first create an entry, and GitBook generates them for you when it saves the site content mapping. Once a space is live, treat its key as permanent:

GitBook Assistant

- To rename a space, change its `title`. The key stays the same.



GitBook Assistant

- To change a space’s URL, change its `path`. The key stays the same.



GitBook Assistant


This example maps English and French spaces to separate directories:

GitBook Assistant

gitbook-docs.yaml

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
$schema: https://api.gitbook.com/gitbook-docs.yaml
site:
  title: Documentation
  structure:
    - type: section
      key: documentation
      title: Documentation
      path: documentation
      children:
        - type: space
          key: docs-en
          title: English
          path: docs
          default: true
          content:
            directory: ./docs/en
            language: en
        - type: space
          key: docs-fr
          title: Français
          path: fr
          content:
            directory: ./docs/fr
            language: fr
```

Show all 24 lines

Configure additional site properties [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration#configure-additional-site-properties)

Use these optional properties to refine your site structure:

GitBook Assistant

Property

Use it for

`type: section-group`

GitBook Assistant

Group related sections under a shared navigation heading.

GitBook Assistant

`description`

GitBook Assistant

Add a description to a section.

GitBook Assistant

`icon`

GitBook Assistant

Add an icon to a section or section group.

GitBook Assistant

`localizedTitle`

GitBook Assistant

Translate a section, section group, or space title.

GitBook Assistant

`localizedDescription`

GitBook Assistant

Translate a section description.

GitBook Assistant

`hidden`

GitBook Assistant

Hide a space from site navigation.

GitBook Assistant

GitBook creates or updates `gitbook-docs.yaml` when it saves the site content mapping.

GitBook Assistant

### Configure a space with .gitbook.yaml[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration\#configure-a-space-with-.gitbook.yaml)

`.gitbook.yaml` configures one space. It lives in that space’s mapped directory. Use it to set the content root, first page, navigation file, and redirects.

GitBook Assistant

The main settings are:

GitBook Assistant

- `root` sets the directory GitBook reads. It defaults to `./`.



GitBook Assistant

- `structure.readme` sets the first page. It defaults to `README.md`.



GitBook Assistant

- `structure.summary` sets the navigation file. It defaults to `SUMMARY.md`.



GitBook Assistant

- `redirects` maps old paths to new paths within the space.



GitBook Assistant


Here is a typical configuration:

GitBook Assistant

.gitbook.yaml

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
root: ./

structure:
  readme: README.md
  summary: SUMMARY.md

redirects:
  previous/page: new-folder/page.md
```

#### Set the content root[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration\#set-the-content-root)

Set `root` when a space’s content lives inside a subdirectory:

GitBook Assistant

.gitbook.yaml

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
root: ./docs/
```

Paths in `.gitbook.yaml` are relative to `root`. With `root: ./docs/`, `structure.summary: ./product/SUMMARY.md` resolves to `./docs/product/SUMMARY.md`.

GitBook Assistant

In a monorepo, `root` only applies inside the mapped space directory. It doesn’t make sibling directories available. For multi-space repository setups, see [Monorepos](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/monorepos).

GitBook Assistant

#### Set the first page and navigation file[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration\#set-the-first-page-and-navigation-file)

Use `structure.readme` and `structure.summary` to set custom file paths:

GitBook Assistant

.gitbook.yaml

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
structure:
  readme: ./product/README.md
  summary: ./product/SUMMARY.md
```

When Git Sync is enabled, manage `README.md` files in your repository. Editing them in GitBook can create conflicts or duplicate pages.

GitBook Assistant

#### Configure redirects[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration\#configure-redirects)

Configure space-level redirects in `.gitbook.yaml`. Redirect paths only apply within that space.

GitBook Assistant

You can also manage site-level redirects in the GitBook app. See [Site redirects](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/site-redirects).

GitBook Assistant

### Configure navigation with SUMMARY.md[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration\#configure-navigation-with-summary.md)

`SUMMARY.md` defines a space’s table of contents. GitBook looks for it in the configured `root` directory.

GitBook Assistant

If GitBook doesn't find `SUMMARY.md`, it infers navigation from your folders and Markdown files. GitBook creates or updates `SUMMARY.md` when you change navigation in GitBook.

GitBook Assistant

Use headings for page groups and nested links for child pages:

GitBook Assistant

SUMMARY.md

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
# Summary

## Product

* [Overview](README.md)
  * [Getting started](getting-started.md)
  * [Configuration](configuration.md)

## Reference

* [API reference](api.md)
```

Each Markdown file can appear once in `SUMMARY.md`. A page can only have one URL in a space.

GitBook Assistant

#### Set navigation labels[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration\#set-navigation-labels)

Add a page link title when the navigation label differs from the page title:

GitBook Assistant

SUMMARY.md

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
# Summary

* [Page main title](page.md "Navigation label")
```

GitBook uses the page link title in the sidebar, pagination, and relative links. Without one, GitBook uses the page title.

GitBook Assistant

Last updated 19 hours ago

Was this helpful?

## Organizing content[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts#organizing-content)
### Docs site[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts#docs-site)
Your docs will be published and available to your selected audience as a website that you can customize with your own branding, analytics and custom domain.

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://gitbook.com/docs/llms.txt). This page is also available as [Markdown](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts.md).

The window is floating on a pastel yellow and pink background](https://gitbook.com/docs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1050631731-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FNkEGS7hzeqa35sMXQZ4X%252Fuploads%252FncL7zGSB2PvZ84M6O3EG%252FEditor%2520and%2520block%2520palette.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dd0115d8f-b63d-45e0-b007-9ce9a8f4bf9b&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=c43868da94709d5034b87218cfe81750&sv=3)![An illustration showing the block palette open in the GitBook editor. The window is floating on a pastel yellow and pink background](https://gitbook.com/docs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1050631731-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FNkEGS7hzeqa35sMXQZ4X%252Fuploads%252F37JXNODvMFd5lJkFftnJ%252FEditor%2520and%2520block%2520palette%2520%281%29.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Df13a2e35-6ad0-497d-855c-862ef47bad12&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f6153b78e4f00a9c5e4840c03d57fe40&sv=3)

## Organizing content[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#organizing-content)

### Section[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#space)

A section is a project that lets you work on a set of related pages. Within a section you can write content, organize your pages with page groups and subpages, install integrations, and more.

GitBook Assistant

Sections belong to a docs site, and you can add as many sections to a docs site as you like. So when you’re building out your content, you can create separate sections for your product documentation, API reference, changelog, help center, and anything else you want to include on your documentation — and publish them all on one docs site.

GitBook Assistant

You may also want to create translated versions of your primary documentation, or separate docs for different versions of your product. Each of these will also have their own section and can be added to your single docs site for users to browse.

GitBook Assistant

#### Group[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#collection)

Groups act like folders within the GitBook app, letting you keep related sections together to make it easier to organize and store your content.

GitBook Assistant

As well as letting you keep content organized, groups also make it easier to manage content-level permissions at scale. You can override organization-level permissions across multiple sections by adding them to a group and setting permissions for the entire group.

GitBook Assistant

### Docs site[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#docs-site)

You can publish your content as a docs site. Your docs will be published and available to your selected audience as a website that you can customize with your own branding, analytics and custom domain.

GitBook Assistant

You can create as many docs sites as you want. They’re all listed in the sidebar and in the Docs sites section of the app, where you can change settings and customization options. You can control all of your docs site’s settings and options in the GitBook app.

GitBook Assistant

The content on your site lives in its sections. When you create a new docs site, you can create a new section, or add existing content. A docs site can contain one section, or multiple sections containing different content — including translations and previous product versions.

GitBook Assistant

## Editing content[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#editing-content)

GitBook’s visual editor lets you use a what-you-see-is-what-you-get (WYSIWYG) interface to add content to a section.

GitBook Assistant

Editing is available on desktop and laptop devices. You can view your organization and content from a smartphone, but editing requires a desktop or laptop.

GitBook Assistant

### Pages[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#pages)

A page is the place where you add, edit and embed content. Pages always live inside a section, and you can add as many pages to a section as you like.

GitBook Assistant

The pages in your section appear in the table of contents on the left-hand side of the editor. Here, you can add new pages, create page groups, and nest pages within other pages to create subpages.

GitBook Assistant

#### Can’t see how to edit or add a page?[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#cant-see-how-to-edit-or-add-a-page)

If your site is published, you’ll need to create a change request before you can make any changes to the content of a section. [Read about change requests below](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts#change-requests).

GitBook Assistant

### Blocks[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#blocks)

GitBook is a block-based editor. That means you can add different kinds of blocks to your page — from standard text and images to more advanced, interactive blocks. Your pages can include any combination of blocks you want, and there’s no limit to the number of blocks you can have on a page.

GitBook Assistant

Block-based editing makes it easy to reorganize your content using drag-and-drop, or add new blocks in the middle of existing content. You can create new blocks using the editor interface, or create and format blocks using Markdown.

GitBook Assistant

Discover all the blocks you can use in GitBook [in the Blocks section](https://gitbook.com/docs/create-content/blocks).

GitBook Assistant

#### Markdown editing[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#markdown-editing)

GitBook’s editor allows you to create and format content blocks using Markdown.

GitBook Assistant

Markdown is a popular markup syntax that’s widely known for its simplicity. GitBook supports it as a keyboard-friendly way to write rich and structured text — all of GitBook’s blocks can be written using Markdown syntax.

GitBook Assistant

You can learn more about Markdown itself by visiting [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/help/).

GitBook Assistant

### Git Sync[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#git-sync)

Git Sync allows teams to synchronize GitHub or GitLab repositories with GitBook and turn Markdown files into beautiful, user-friendly docs. Once set up, it keeps all your content synchronized between the GitBook app and your codebase.

GitBook Assistant

Git Sync is bi-directional, so changes you make in GitBook’s visual editor are automatically synced — as are any commits made on GitHub or GitLab. This allows developers to commit directly from GitHub or GitLab while other team members edit and leave feedback on changes directly in GitBook.

GitBook Assistant

Git Sync also unlocks many other useful workflows in your GitBook docs, such as batch changes, linting, and more. Learn more in [our Git Sync section](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync).

GitBook Assistant

## The editing flow[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#the-editing-flow)

### Change requests[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#change-requests)

A change request is a [**branch**](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Branching-Branches-in-a-Nutshell) of your main content that you can use to make concurrent edits, while maintaining your version history. It will feel familiar to anyone who uses pull requests in GitHub or merge requests in GitLab.

GitBook Assistant

If you want to edit the content on your published docs site, you’ll first need to open a change request in your section.

GitBook Assistant

In a change request, you can add, edit and delete content in a section, then request a review from your team and merge your changes into your main content to update your published docs site.

GitBook Assistant

#### Branching in brief[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#branching-in-brief)

Opening a change request creates a copy of your content at that specific moment in time, sometimes called a ‘branch’. Any changes you make will not appear in your main content until you choose to merge your change request.

GitBook Assistant

The advantage of branching is that your teammates can create, edit and merge their own change requests at the same time as you without stepping on each other’s toes. And if someone edits the same content as you, GitBook will guide you through resolving any conflicts before you merge.

GitBook Assistant

#### Reviews[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#reviews)

Reviews encourage oversight and help improve the quality and accuracy of your documentation.

GitBook Assistant

You can request a review on your change request before you merge and make the changes live on your docs site. Adding a title and description to your change request gives your reviewers some context.

GitBook Assistant

Reviewers can view the diff for your change request, which highlights everything that’s new, changed or deleted in your change request. They can also leave feedback right on the page using the built-in comments feature -- then approve your change request, or ask for more changes to be made.

GitBook Assistant

#### Merging[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#merging)

Merging a change request will add all the content in your change request into the main branch of content — and those changes will also go live on your docs site.

GitBook Assistant

When you merge your change request, it also creates a new version in the section’s version history.

GitBook Assistant

## Publishing documentation[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#publishing-documentation)

When you publish your content as a [docs site](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts#docs-site), you can add more content to your site, change the audience, and customize its look, feel and other settings.

GitBook Assistant

### Structuring your docs site[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#structuring-your-docs-site)

If you want to add extra content to your site, there are two options for you to use, each designed for different use cases: sections and variants.

GitBook Assistant

#### Sections in your site structure[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#site-section)

Sections let you add **multiple different types of documentation to a single docs site**. For example, you could use a single docs site and use it to host your product docs, API reference, help center and changelog — as we do on this docs site.

GitBook Assistant

When you add new sections, you build out the navigation bar at the top of your site, with each section getting its own entry on the bar. You can also keep sections together in a [group](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts#collection) to create a drop-down menu in your navigation bar — ideal for adding hierarchy to your site.

GitBook Assistant

#### Variant[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#variant)

Variants are designed to let you add **multiple versions of the same documentation to a single docs site**. For example, you might want to localize your entire documentation into multiple languages, or document previous versions of your product for users that haven’t updated.

GitBook Assistant

Your end users can switch between these variants on your docs site using the language picker or the variant picker at the top of the table of contents on the left-hand side of your site.

GitBook Assistant

![A screenshot of the Roboflow Documentation site, with a navigation bar along the top and an open drop-down menu at the top of the table of contents showing different language variants for the site.](https://gitbook.com/docs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1050631731-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FNkEGS7hzeqa35sMXQZ4X%252Fuploads%252FD4oCABc0YRJAFzaaVBpn%252Fstructure%25402x.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D4c4dd0df-8e8e-40e7-8a57-e9791d337c8f&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=cad6ccb85e2111b9ec187bfcbc3b12a2&sv=3)

Sections create a navigation bar along the top of your site, while users can switch between variants using a menu in the table of contents.

### Site audience[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#site-audience)

You can choose who will see your documentation when you publish it. The default for new sites is for them to be published publicly, and indexed by search engines.

GitBook Assistant

However, if you want more control over who can access your site, you can choose to limit the audience using **share links** or **authenticated access**.

GitBook Assistant

With share links, you can share you content privately with customers or partners without needing to invite them to your organization by creating a private link and sharing it with them directly. Anyone with the link can access your site.

GitBook Assistant

If you want even more control, authenticated access allows you to publish your content while requiring authentication from any visitors who want to view it. When enabled, GitBook lets your authentication provider handle who has access to the content. This is ideal for private content or for publishing an internal knowledge base that should only be accessible by members of your team.

GitBook Assistant

You can also control who sees individual pages or blocks using a feature called adaptive content. Once set up, it will show or hide content based on user attributes that you decide upon. Read more in [the Adaptive content pages](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/adaptive-content).

GitBook Assistant

### Site customization[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#site-customization)

GitBook includes built-in customization options for docs sites, helping you match the look and feel of your documentation to your product or brand.

GitBook Assistant

Even if you don’t apply any customizations, your docs will look great as they are. But you have the option to customize logos, icons, and colors, add custom fonts, or choose from some built-in themes that help your docs look as great as your product.

GitBook Assistant

![An illustration showing five docs sites hosted in GitBook, each with distinct visual customizations](https://gitbook.com/docs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1050631731-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FNkEGS7hzeqa35sMXQZ4X%252Fuploads%252FPHDUX2Kbmd9wwUBpJqst%252Fcustomization-demo.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D7586ba34-9cd2-47ee-9169-81b73dd40923&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=dbd1a4c20aeb6b03b839ac4bf756c116&sv=3)

You can customize your documentation to match your brand with your own logos, colors, fonts, images and much more.

### SEO and AI optimizations[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#seo-and-ai-optimizations)

Documentation published in GitBook is automatically optimized for search (SEO) and for AI systems like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google AI Overview (GEO). These are handled in the back end, so all you need to do is write content that includes the keywords and terms you want to target.

GitBook Assistant

Pages pull metadata from each page’s title and description, and your content is formatted to be responsive. GitBook automatically creates a sitemap based on your table of contents, and pages are cached and served via our global CDN to improve performance. All of these help your documentation to rank high in search engines.

GitBook Assistant

Likewise, GitBook also optimizes for AI tools following all the industry standards as they quickly evolve.

GitBook Assistant

GitBook automatically creates .md versions of every page, which makes it easier for large-language models (LLMs) to parse. We also automatically expose a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for every published site, giving AI tools a structured way to discover and retrieve your docs as resources — no scraping required. Plus, your site also generates `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` designed for AI ingestion.

GitBook Assistant

## Team management[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#team-management)

### Organization[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#organization)

A GitBook organization contains all of the content and docs sites for an individual company. With your single account, you can be a member of one or many organizations and switch between them using the organization menu at the top of the sidebar.

GitBook Assistant

### Members[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#members)

Members are individual users within your organization. You can have as many members as you like in an organization, each with permissions suited to their specific access needs.

GitBook Assistant

#### Permissions[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/concepts\#permissions)

Permissions let you decide on the access level of your organization’s members. When a member joins your organization, you assign them a role — such as Editor or Viewer. These roles define their permissions for all of your organization’s content. But you can also override these permissions at a content level. For example:

GitBook Assistant

- You can give someone with the Viewer role editing access to one particular piece of content



GitBook Assistant

- You can limit access to specific confidential or private content and only grant access to certain members of your organization.



GitBook Assistant


Read more on [the Permissions and inheritance page](https://gitbook.com/docs/collaborate/member-management/permissions-and-inheritance).

GitBook Assistant

Last updated 22 days ago

Was this helpful?

web.title: Enabling GitHub Sync | GitBook Documentation
web.description: Sync your GitHub repo with GitBook. Select the branch that GitBook syncs with. Before you start the initial sync, confirm the repository, ...
web.markdown:
[New: The GitBook MCP server is here.\\
\\
Connect your AI agent](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/gitbook-mcp)

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://gitbook.com/docs/llms.txt). This page is also available as [Markdown](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync.md).

This guide will take you through setting up your GitBook site with a repo on GitHub.

GitBook Assistant

![A GitBook screenshot showing GitHub Sync configuration options](https://gitbook.com/docs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1050631731-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FNkEGS7hzeqa35sMXQZ4X%252Fuploads%252Fr60MP09ALOfZOwCXOgKz%252FGit%2520Sync%2520-%2520GitHub.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D4289a896-e828-44d7-8c1a-8a752f8eaa4c&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=eb796f692619baa479306764d88f39bb&sv=3)

GitHub Sync configuration options.

1

### Open Git Sync for your site[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#open-git-sync-for-your-site)

From your site, open Git Sync in the sidebar.

GitBook Assistant

2

### Connect GitHub[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#connect-github)

Connect the GitHub account that has access to the repository you want to sync.

GitBook Assistant

If you see a **'Potential duplicated accounts'** error message at this step, this means your GitHub account is already linked with another GitBook user account.

GitBook Assistant

To help you identify which accounts are linked, you will have to log out from this session and log in using the sign-in with GitHub method.

GitBook Assistant

If you already know your GitBook account associated with GitHub you can log into that user account and unlink your GitHub account (done in settings) before logging back in and linking your current account.

GitBook Assistant

Read more on our [troubleshooting page](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#potential-duplicated-accounts-when-signing-in).

GitBook Assistant

3

### Select a repository and branch[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#select-a-repository-and-branch)

Under **Source repository**, select the repository that contains your documentation. Select the branch that GitBook syncs with. If the branch doesn’t exist, GitBook creates it during the initial sync.

GitBook Assistant

**Can’t find your repository?** If you can't find your repository in the list, make sure that you've installed the [GitBook GitHub app](https://github.com/apps/gitbook-com) in the right scope (i.e. your personal account or the GitHub org where the repository lives). You should also check that you’ve configured the correct repository access in the GitBook GitHub app.

GitBook Assistant

4

### Choose an initial sync direction[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#choose-an-initial-sync-direction)

Choose the source of truth for the initial sync. Select **Swap direction** if the repository content should replace the GitBook content.

GitBook Assistant

**GitHub → GitBook can replace your section’s content.** If you select an empty repository, GitBook can replace your section with the repository’s empty content.

GitBook Assistant

Before you start the initial sync, confirm the repository, branch, and direction. Make sure the destination content is safe to replace.

GitBook Assistant

5

### Set the project directory[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#set-the-project-directory)

If your documentation lives in a subdirectory, enter it under **Project directory**. GitBook stores your site’s `docs.yaml` file in this directory. Use this configuration if your docs live within a [monorepo](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/monorepos).

GitBook Assistant

6

### Map your spaces[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#map-your-spaces)

Under **Content mapping**, assign each space to a directory in the repository. Use `./` for paths relative to the project directory. Use `/` for paths from the repository root. Newly linked spaces sync automatically.

GitBook Assistant

7

### Review advanced options[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#review-advanced-options)

If needed, configure agent instruction files, a commit message template, or fork previews.

GitBook Assistant

8

### Sync your site[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#sync-your-site)

Click **Sync** to start the initial sync.

GitBook Assistant

9

### Write and commit[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#write-and-commit)

Merge a change request in GitBook to commit its changes to GitHub. Commits to GitHub sync back to GitBook.

GitBook Assistant

#### Exclude a space from site-wide Git Sync[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/enabling-github-sync\#exclude-a-space-from-site-wide-git-sync)

In the site’s Git Sync content mapping, click the remove icon next to the space you want to exclude. You can then configure Git Sync from that space.

GitBook Assistant

If the site already has Git Sync, GitBook asks you to choose a scope:

GitBook Assistant

- Select the site’s repository and branch to add the space to site-wide Git Sync.



GitBook Assistant

- Select an independent repository and branch to configure Space Git Sync.



GitBook Assistant


If the site doesn’t use Git Sync, GitBook configures Git Sync independently for the space.

GitBook Assistant

To configure Git Sync for a single space, in the space you want to sync, click **Set up** next to **Git Sync** in the [space header](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/gitbook-ui#space-header). From the provider list, click **GitHub Sync**.

GitBook Assistant

The GitHub app that powers our GitHub integration is currently not available to customers on GitHub Enterprise Server instances.

GitBook Assistant

Last updated 9 days ago

Was this helpful?

web.title: Troubleshooting | GitBook Documentation
web.description: 4 days ago · Use these solutions to resolve common Git Sync and repository issues. Expand a topic to find the relevant checks and next steps.
web.markdown:
[New: The GitBook MCP server is here.\\
\\
Connect your AI agent](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/gitbook-mcp)

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://gitbook.com/docs/llms.txt). This page is also available as [Markdown](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting.md).

Use these solutions to resolve common Git Sync and repository issues. Expand a topic to find the relevant checks and next steps.

GitBook Assistant

### Sync errors and access[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting\#sync-errors-and-access)

Error when pushing to a repository with a protected branch [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#error-when-pushing-to-a-repository-with-a-protected-branch)

This error occurs when your Git branch is protected:

GitBook Assistant

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
Error: Missing permissions to push to the refs/heads/main protected branch. Check your branch configuration on your git provider.
```

Git Sync requires the GitBook app to push changes to your repository without restrictions, including during setup. Allow the GitBook app to bypass branch protections for the sync to work.

GitBook Assistant

GitBook supports these branch protections, as long as the app is allowed to bypass them:

GitBook Assistant

- Require a pull request before merging



GitBook Assistant

- Restrict who can push to matching branches



GitBook Assistant


In GitHub, open your repository's branch protection settings and allow `gitbook-com` to bypass those restrictions.

GitBook Assistant

Git Sync status shows an unexpected error [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#git-sync-status-shows-an-unexpected-error)

**If the error appeared when merging a change request in GitBook:** create a new change request with a small change — such as adding a word — and merge it. This retriggers the sync and GitBook exports all content again, including the changes from the failed sync.

GitBook Assistant

**If the error appeared when merging a commit from GitHub or GitLab:** create a new commit in your repository with a small change. When it merges, GitBook imports all content from the repository again, including the changes from the failed sync.

GitBook Assistant

**If the error appeared during first-time setup:** remove the GitHub or GitLab integration, enable it again in your section, and go through the setup process once more.

GitBook Assistant

If none of these steps help, [contact support](https://gitbook.com/docs/help/contact-support).

GitBook Assistant

Git authentication failed [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#git-authentication-failed)

This message appears when you attempt to push to a repository that hasn't granted GitBook access. In that case, syncing from your repository to GitBook works, but not the other way — and your repositories may not be listed correctly.

GitBook Assistant

For GitHub, grant access in your GitHub settings: open **Manage Organization → Integrations → Applications**, click **Configure** next to GitBook, and select the repositories the GitBook app can access.

GitBook Assistant

For GitLab, make sure your access token is configured with `api`, `read_repository`, and `write_repository` access.

GitBook Assistant

GitHub preview isn't showing [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#github-preview-isnt-showing)

If your GitHub preview is not showing, it might be because your GitSync integration was configured before January 2022. Versions of GitSync configured before this date do not include GitHub Preview.

GitBook Assistant

You should have received a notification requesting you to accept an updated permission request to enable read-only access to PRs.

GitBook Assistant

In case you did not receive the notification, to troubleshoot you need to update to the new version:

GitBook Assistant

1. Uninstall the GitSync integration from your organization.



GitBook Assistant

2. Reinstall the new version with the updated permissions.



GitBook Assistant


Note that uninstalling the GitSync integration will require reconfiguring the integration again on any sections it was previously connected to.

GitBook Assistant

### Repository content and structure[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting\#repository-content-and-structure)

Git Sync file size limitations [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#git-sync-file-size-limitations)

Git Sync limits individual file sizes to a maximum of 100MB. To improve performance and synchronization speed, optimize the size of files and assets in your repository.

GitBook Assistant

My table of contents isn't correctly structured [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#my-table-of-contents-isnt-correctly-structured)

Your `SUMMARY.md` file mirrors your table of contents on GitBook — the way it's structured is reflected in your content. Make sure the file reflects the structure you want to see in your documentation. See [Content configuration](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration#summary) for the expected format.

GitBook Assistant

My links to another space return 404 after I edited `gitbook-docs.yaml` [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#my-links-to-another-space-return-404-after-i-edited-gitbook-docs.yaml)

Cross-space links resolve through space IDs. Git Sync identifies each space in `gitbook-docs.yaml` by its `key`, so changing a space’s key replaces that space: GitBook creates a new one, imports your content into it from the mapped directory, and leaves the original space in your organization, detached from the site.

GitBook Assistant

Your pages come back, but the space ID changes. Links, cards, and `SUMMARY.md` entries that point at the old ID break.

GitBook Assistant

The new ID is permanent. Restoring the original key doesn’t bring the old one back — it creates another new space with another new ID. Repoint the affected references at the current space, and add [site redirects](https://gitbook.com/docs/publish/site-redirects) for the published URLs that changed.

GitBook Assistant

The original space is still in your organization if you need something from it that isn’t in your repository. [Contact support](https://gitbook.com/docs/help/contact-support) with the original space ID if you can’t find it.

GitBook Assistant

Does Git Sync also sync pull requests? [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#does-git-sync-also-sync-pull-requests)

No. Creating a pull request in GitHub or GitLab doesn't create a change request in GitBook, and creating a change request in GitBook doesn't create a pull request in your repository.

GitBook Assistant

### Common Git Sync issues[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting\#common-git-sync-issues)

I have a GitHub sync error [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#i-have-a-github-sync-error)

#### Create README files in your repository[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting\#create-readme-files-in-your-repository)

When Git Sync is enabled, be careful not to create readme files through the GitBook UI. Creating readme files through the GitBook UI:

GitBook Assistant

- Creates duplicate README files in your repository



GitBook Assistant

- Causes rendering conflicts between GitBook and GitHub



GitBook Assistant

- May break builds and deployment processes



GitBook Assistant

- Results in unpredictable file precedence



GitBook Assistant


This includes files named README.md, readme.md, Readme.md, and README (without extension). Instead, remember to manage your README file directly in your git repository.

GitBook Assistant

#### Still facing errors?[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting\#still-facing-errors)

Make sure that:‌

GitBook Assistant

- Your repository **has a**`README.md` **file** at its root (or at the `root` folder specified in your `.gitbook.yaml`) that was created directly in your git repository. This file is required and is used as the homepage for your documentation. For more details, refer to our [content configuration](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration).



GitBook Assistant

- If you have YAML frontmatters in your Markdown files, make sure they are valid using a [linter](http://www.yamllint.com/).​



GitBook Assistant


GitBook isn't using my `docs` folder [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#gitbook-isnt-using-my-docs-folder)

By default, GitBook uses the root of the repository as a starting point. A specific directory can be specified to scope the markdown files. Take a look at our documentation on [content configuration](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration) for more details.‌

GitBook Assistant

GitBook is creating new Markdown files [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#gitbook-is-creating-new-markdown-files)

**When synchronizing and editing from GitBook** with an existing Git repository, GitBook may create new markdown files instead of using the existing ones.‌ This is done to ensure GitBook doesn't overrite files that existed in your repository before.

GitBook Assistant

Redirects aren't working correctly [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#redirects-arent-working-correctly)

The YAML file needs to be correctly formatted for the redirects to work. Errors such as incorrect indentation or whitespace can result in your redirects not working. [Validating your YAML file](https://www.yamllint.com/) can ensure that the redirects will work smoothly.

GitBook Assistant

When setting redirects, do not add any leading slashes. For example, trying to redirect to `./misc/support.md` will not work.

GitBook Assistant

It's also important to consider that as long as a page exists for a path, GitBook won’t be looking for a possible redirect. So if you're setting up a redirect for an old page to a new one, you will need to remove the old page in order for the redirect to work.

GitBook Assistant

My repository isn't listed [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#my-repository-isnt-listed)

#### GitHub repositories[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting\#github-repositories)

Make sure that you have installed the GitBook GitHub app to the correct locations (when installing the app, you can choose to install it to your personal GitHub, or to any organization you have permissions for) and that you have given the app the correct repository permissions.

GitBook Assistant

#### GitLab repositories[Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting\#gitlab-repositories)

Make sure that your access token has been configured with the following access:

GitBook Assistant

- `api`



GitBook Assistant

- `read_repository`



GitBook Assistant

- `write_repository`



GitBook Assistant


Nothing happens after I add a file to my repository [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#nothing-happens-after-i-add-a-file-to-my-repository)

**This section specifically addresses problems when a**`SUMMARY.md` **file already exists**

GitBook Assistant

If your repository does not include a `SUMMARY.md` file, GitBook will automatically create one upon the first sync. This means that if you edited your content from GitBook at least once after setting up Git sync, GitBook should have created this file automatically.‌

GitBook Assistant

If after updating your repository by adding or modifying a markdown file, you do not see the update reflected on GitBook and the sidebar doesn’t indicate an error during the sync, your modified file(s) is probably not listed in [your `SUMMARY.md` file](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/content-configuration#summary).‌

GitBook Assistant

This could either be because you created the file manually, or because you made an edit on GitBook and the GitBook to Git export phase of the sync created it for you.

GitBook Assistant

The content of this file mirrors your [table of contents](https://gitbook.com/docs/reference/gitbook-ui#table-of-contents) on GitBook and is used during the Git to GitBook import phase of the sync to recreate your table of contents and re-conciliate upcoming updates from the repository with your existing content on GitBook.‌

GitBook Assistant

If after ensuring that all your files are included in the `SUMMARY.md` file there’s still nothing happening on GitBook, don’t hesitate to [contact support](https://gitbook.com/docs/help/contact-support) for assistance.

GitBook Assistant

I have duplicate accounts when signing in [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#i-have-duplicate-accounts-when-signing-in)

This error usually occurs when the GitHub account that you use to set up the sync is already associated with a different GitBook user account.

GitBook Assistant

A good way to identify which GitBook account the GitHub account is already linked to is:

GitBook Assistant

1. Log out from your current GitBook user session (i.e. `name@email.com`)



GitBook Assistant

2. Log out from any GitHub user sessions.



GitBook Assistant

3. Go to [the Log in page](https://app.gitbook.com/login).



GitBook Assistant

4. Select the "Sign in with GitHub" option.



GitBook Assistant

5. Enter your GitHub credentials.



GitBook Assistant

6. Once logged in, go to [the account settings](https://app.gitbook.com/account) and either:



GitBook Assistant





1. Unlink the account from the "Third-party Login > GitHub" section in the Personal setting



      GitBook Assistant

2. Delete the account altogether if you do not need it.



      GitBook Assistant


7. Log out from the session.



GitBook Assistant

8. Log back in using your `name@email.com` GitBook account.



GitBook Assistant

9. Try to set up Git Sync again.



GitBook Assistant


Unsafe files are blocking Git Sync [Direct link to heading](https://gitbook.com/docs/docs-as-code/git-sync/troubleshooting#unsafe-files-are-blocking-git-sync)

Git Sync can fail if your space contains files that GitBook considers unsafe to export (e.g. `.js`).

GitBook Assistant

You may see an error like:

GitBook Assistant

> `File "<filename>" cannot be exported as it is considered unsafe`
>
> GitBook Assistant

Unsafe files must be removed from the GitBook space, not just from the Git repository.

GitBook Assistant

1. Create a change request in the affected space



GitBook Assistant

2. Open the **Files** tab



GitBook Assistant

3. Delete the unsafe file(s)



GitBook Assistant

4. Merge the change request



GitBook Assistant


Once the unsafe files are removed from the space, Git Sync should resume normally.

GitBook Assistant

Last updated 3 days ago

Was this helpful?
